known_limitations: PID identity race (independent-audit acceptance blocker, commit 0a71cd9): the pre-remediation stop validated identity through a transient handle and left the PID unpinned for a measured ~3.031 s (reproduced here at 3.063 s) across the health probe, then signalled and terminated by raw PID. CLOSED by this remediation - see process_identity_race. Residual: the instant between the process object being freed and OpenProcess being called cannot be removed, but it is fail-closed, because the authorizing identity is read back through the pinned handle.
The specific handle holder on the owner's machine is UNPROVEN; the fix is correct under either surviving explanation.
process_alive() remains true-but-not-conclusive on Windows; it is retained only where False is the load-bearing answer, and its docstring records the limitation.
An unproven stop deliberately leaves the PID record in place, so a genuinely-exited console whose exit was unprovable is re-signalled by the next Stop, still fully identity-gated.

PROCESS_EXITED_RUNTIME_STATE_STALE reports a QUALIFIED success to the owner - the process did stop, but the launcher could not remove its own runtime record, and the owner is told so before starting again. runtime_state_cleared=false and the stop_state are preserved.
The graceful console-break is still expected to fail for a detached child on Windows, so a healthy stop costs about 3.3 s via escalation. Unchanged baseline behaviour.
The committed suite uses stand-in child processes rather than the console itself, to stay offline and port-free; a live launcher run is recorded in live_launcher_run.
An identity refusal clears NO runtime state, by design. A genuinely stale record is reclaimed by Start's stale-PID sweep, not by a Stop that could not prove what it was looking at.

process_identity_race.defect: Stop validated the recorded process start token through a TRANSIENT handle, then left the PID unpinned across the health probe, and only afterwards opened the verifier handle. Graceful signalling used the raw PID, and hard termination opened a SECOND handle by raw PID and terminated through it without validating the creation token through that exact handle. Between the identity read and the handle acquisition the process object could be freed and the PID reassigned, so a signal could reach a process that was never verified.

independent_reproduction.mechanism: the recorded PID was released and reassigned during the unpinned interval; hard escalation then opened a PROCESS_TERMINATE handle on the replacement and terminated it

measured_exposure_window.agreement: same phenomenon, dominated by HEALTH_REQUEST_TIMEOUT = 3.0; the difference is scheduling jitter

measured_exposure_window.method: instrumented start_token and exit_verifier seams around a health endpoint that accepts the TCP connection and never answers, so the probe runs to the full HEALTH_REQUEST_TIMEOUT - the unhealthy/unresponsive console case

pinning_guarantee.claim: From the moment the verifier handle is open AND its handle-derived creation token has matched the recorded token, until stop() returns, that PID cannot become a different process.
pinning_guarantee.does_not_cover: any instant before the handle exists - nothing pins a PID before a handle to it is open
pinning_guarantee.scope: exactly that period, and exactly that validated handle
pinning_guarantee.why_withdrawn: the handle was opened after the identity check and after the health probe, so it did not cover the interval the sentence claimed, and hard escalation reopened a handle by raw PID
pinning_guarantee.withdrawn_claim: Windows cannot recycle that PID while the stop is in flight, so the escalation is guaranteed to reach the same process object whose identity was proven

pre_remediation_sequence.note: THE EXPOSURE WINDOW - up to HEALTH_REQUEST_TIMEOUT = 3.0 s
handle finally opened; pinning starts only here
graceful signal issued by raw PID
SECOND handle opened by raw PID, terminated through with NO identity re-check

remediation.1_pinned_handle_opened_first: open_exit_verifier(pid) runs before the health probe, before any other delay and before anything is signalled
remediation.2_token_read_through_that_exact_handle: WindowsExitVerifier.__init__ calls GetProcessTimes(handle) on the handle it just opened and stores start_token
remediation.3_compared_with_recorded_token: Launcher._pinned_identity compares recorded, handle-derived and raw-PID tokens
remediation.5_handle_held_for_the_complete_stop: closed in a finally that wraps the whole operation, including the post-stop port and health diagnostics
remediation.6_termination_handle_validated_separatel: terminate_process_result(..., expect_token=) opens PROCESS_TERMINATE | PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION, re-reads the creation token through THAT handle, and returns TERMINATION_IDENTITY_MISMATCH without issuing any kill when it differs
remediation.graceful_signal_note: CTRL_BREAK_EVENT signals a console process GROUP by number and has no handle form. It is issued only after the pinned handle is open and its token has matched; Windows cannot recycle a PID while that handle is held, which is what makes the number safe to use.

residual.description: Between the kernel freeing a process object and OpenProcess being called there remains an instant in which the recorded PID could already belong to another process. No API opens a handle without naming the PID, so this cannot be removed.
residual.why_harmless: nothing is signalled on the strength of the number. The handle is opened first and the authorizing identity is read back through it, so a reassigned PID yields a non-matching token and the stop refuses without signalling, terminating or clearing state.

root_cause.mechanism: OpenProcess + GetProcessTimes succeed on a terminated, handle-referenced process object; Windows frees the object only after exit AND full handle release.
root_cause.statement: process_alive() is not an exit test on Windows. It answers 'is this PID still addressable?', which remains true for an already-exited process for as long as ANY handle to the process object is open. _await_exit() polled exactly that, so a console the kernel had already reported as terminated was reported to the owner as still running, and the full 15 s budget was consumed before CONSOLE_DID_NOT_STOP.

surviving_explanations: third-party handle holder (AV / indexer / WMI / conhost)
unproven_and_declared.why_it_does_not_matter: The launcher's own topology releases in 0.25 s on this machine (probe_real_topology case 1), so a third party held the reference, or the kernel teardown was genuinely slow. The accepted baseline cannot distinguish those two, and that inability IS the defect. Exit is now proven through a handle the launcher holds itself, so neither explanation can produce a false CONSOLE_DID_NOT_STOP.
